# Decision-aware cost of the gap-resolved ISC observable (generated by decision_cost.py)

CAS(12,11), THC qubitization: 193 logical qubits, 3.25e+03 Toffolis per walk step, λ' = λ + |E0 − c0| = 15.9 + 3.46 = 19.4 Ha, filter width Δ = 0.072 eV, filter degree d = (0.554 ln(1/ε) + -0.106) λ'/Δ (fitted to our filters). Coherent S1 preparation (spin-adapted sum of CSFs + eigenstate filter, flag success γ² = 0.5 folded into the good state) 2.4e+07, H_SO basis rotation 4.5e+03, one QPE for E(S1) at 0.5 mHa 4.4e+08 Toffolis. Success probability γ² k_ISC/K′, K′ = (2π/ħ) α_SO² ρ_max. Confidence 0.95 per decision. MLAE constant c = 45.0 (95th percentile, from ae_demo.py).

Reference, arXiv:2512.15889 (Orig-BDP, N = 11): ISC proxy 7.96e+07 Toffolis × 483 shots = 3.8e+10 at fixed additive precision (not a decision; the proxy gives no absolute rate).

δ = 0.05 per decision. For a campaign of N dyes with a family-wise error δ, replace δ by δ/N. For canonical QAE (median of runs) this raises the number of runs from 16 to 40 for N = 100 (×2.5); for MLAE the tail has not been characterized. The D2 call counts assume that the margin to the threshold is known (an oracle margin); an adaptive test adds a logarithmic overhead. With r = 0.4 instead of 0.2 the D1 MLAE costs halve. Sensitivity: γ² = 0.1 / 0.9 multiplies the calls by 2.24 / 0.75; an S1 filter gap of 0.1 eV instead of 0.5 eV (no spin-adapted trial state) raises C_S1 from 2.4e+07 to 1.2e+08.
